capabilities.description: Canonical 13-field address resolution (planetary, dimension, gate, line, color, tone, base, degree, minute, second, arc, zodiac, house).

verification_evidence.summary: Authority executed for real: YNIV parts resolved then translated to spine form and validated by spine.validateCanonicalAddress -> canonicalAddressKey 'planetary=4|dimension=Being|gate=42|line=5|color=3|tone=6|base=4|degree=248|minute=19|second=52|arcUnit=11|zodiac=6|house=8'; contract arc<->spine arcAxis mapping still NOT translated (documented)

known_limitations: Spine schema names field 11 'arcAxis' (arcUnit 1-99 + axis); contract field 'arc' is served by the kimi DMS codec instead. Spine structure metadata is preserved via ADDRESS_STRUCTURE.
authority-by-designation (Amendment C); automated validation of contract-shaped addresses blocked on arcAxis<->arc field-mapping reconciliation

selection_hints.preferred_when: ALWAYS as final validator: completed addresses (from any constructor, incl. kimi DMS codec) should be validated against execution-spine canonical schema before being treated as canonical. NOTE: spine field 11 is 'arcAxis' (arcUnit 1-99 + axis) vs contract/DMS 'arc' (arc-seconds); validation adapter for this field mapping is a pending reconciliation item, so authority is designated but automated spine-validation is not yet wired.

conclusions.conclusion: DESIGNATED canonical-address AUTHORITY (Amendment C): its schema/validator decides canonicity of completed 13-field addresses. Other address providers construct/resolve parts; completed addresses SHOULD be validated against execution-spine before being called canonical.
conclusions.reason: Amendment C ruling: address authority and address construction are distinct roles; the execution-spine holds the full canonical spine (incl. arcAxis/ADDRESS_STRUCTURE) and must remain the arbiter.
